cells.tense: You're here right now, at the start of seeing clearly, and you know you're holding the pen.
cells.ask: Shine today because you are light, not to prove it — and notice what that feeds next.
cells.core:
You're seeing clearly, and you're not trying to make it mean more than it does. That first cut of clarity is in your hands — you decide what it's for, and it's not out to prove anything. It shows in how you talk, what you notice, what you choose not to name yet.

The direction you're leaning toward is one you recognized, not one you were handed. When it's going well, this is a quiet kind of pull — you don't need to argue for it, you just stay oriented toward it and let that be enough. What that leans you into next is bigger than it looks right now.
cells.sheetLine: You're seeing clearly and leaning toward what you recognized, not what you were handed.
cells.place: at the point where a person knows which way to lean

cells.tense: You're living ahead of the moment, bracing for something that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Let one thing be unfinished today without reaching for the ending in your head.
cells.core:
You're trying to see the whole thing before it happens. Every conversation gets run forward, checked against a version that isn't here yet, and the trying is crowding out the seeing. That first cut of clarity becomes a knife you keep sharpening instead of using.

When it's going well, the pull toward what you actually want doesn't need managing. It's a direction you walk, one step at a time. You notice what you notice, and you move — the wanting is the fuel, not the problem. Today, let one thing stay open. Put the ending down and be in the room you're actually in, with the person who's actually here.
cells.sheetLine: You're trying to see the end before you've walked to it.
cells.place: at the point where a person knows which way to lean

cells.tense: You're still standing in front of a door you already walked through, looking back.
cells.ask: Choose one small completed thing today and let the choosing come from clarity, not from pushing.
cells.core:
The seeing came and you didn't trust it. Acting on what you saw stopped being something you did, and the stopping has outlasted whatever set it off. You can still read what's in front of you — the perception hasn't gone anywhere — but you haven't been stepping from it toward the thing you want.

When this is working, the wanting does the pulling and you do the walking. One clear yes at a time, no forcing, no heat. The direction stays lit even when you don't move on it, and that steadiness is what's still here waiting for you. What's waiting is a single thing you already know is finished being decided. Choose it from that clarity, and let the choosing carry you forward.
cells.sheetLine: The seeing came and you stopped acting on it.

cells.tense: You've got the pen down while the page in front of you is being written, right now.
cells.ask: Name one thing you already see clearly, out loud, once — and let that be enough.
cells.core:
You're already seeing what's in front of you — you notice things, you read the room, you know which way is which. But you're talking about it like it's something that's happening to you rather than something you're doing. The perceiving is running. The claiming isn't.

When the light is on and you own it, this is just shining — no proof, no performance, no need to be right. The lean is still there and it's still yours, and the seeing gets to be something you did rather than something that landed on you. Start by naming one thing you already see out loud. You'll recognize the rest as it comes.
cells.sheetLine: You're already seeing it. Saying so is the part that's missing.
